title: Approximately Optimal Approximate Reinforcement Learning
headline: Don't jump to the greedy policy; blend toward it just enough that each round is a guaranteed improvement, and you reach a near-optimal policy in a number of rounds that depends on how good your value estimates are, never on how big the world is.
abstract: In order to solve realistic reinforcement learning problems, it is critical that approximate algorithms be used. In this paper, we present the conservative policy iteration algorithm which finds an "approximately" optimal policy, given access to a restart distribution (which draws the next state from a particular distribution) and an approximate greedy policy chooser. Crudely, the greedy policy chooser outputs a policy that usually chooses actions with the largest state-action values of the current policy, ie it outputs an "approximate" greedy policy. This greedy policy chooser can be implemented using standard value function approximation techniques. Under these assumptions, our algorithm: (1) is guaranteed to improve a performance metric (2) is guaranteed to terminate in a "small" number of timesteps and (3) returns an "approximately" optimal policy. The quantified statements of (2) and (3) depend on the quality of the greedy policy chooser, but not explicitly on the size of the state space.

images.alt: A pixel explorer on a hillside with a short clay-orange step-arrow nudging a little uphill to a check mark, beside a long thin arrow that leaps high and tumbles down to land lower than the start, showing that a small careful step is a sure climb while a confident greedy leap can drop you below where you began because the ground shifts as you move.
images.caption: A small careful step is a sure climb; a greedy leap can land you lower than you started, because the ground shifts as you move.

images.alt: A large pitcher pouring a wide sage stream and a small clay-orange bottle adding a thin splash into one measuring cup, with a dial between them, showing that the updated policy is mostly the current habit with only a small fraction of the greedy move mixed in.
images.caption: The new policy is mostly the current one with a small splash of the greedy move blended in.

images.alt: A clay-orange arc that rises to a flag at its peak then bends down into a dark crevasse on the right, showing that the guaranteed gain grows with the step size up to a sweet spot and then turns into a loss once the step is too big.
images.caption: The guaranteed gain rises to a sweet-spot step size, then a too-big step turns the sure gain into a loss.

images.alt: A grid map with a small house in the bottom-left corner and grey fog over the far corners, then clay-orange restart flags scattered across the far cells lifting the fog, showing that practicing only from the start leaves rarely-reached states in the dark while scattering the starting points reveals the whole map.
images.caption: Practicing only from the start leaves far states in fog; scattering the restart points reveals the whole map.
